paras: The Americus whipping and ax-handle assault took place on Saturday, 23 August 1890, in Americus, Georgia, when a white woman whipped a Black girl and her husband, a storekeeper, struck the girl's father on the head with an ax handle. Four or five warrants were issued two days later, and the episode is known only from a single paragraph in the Savannah Morning News.
According to the Savannah paper, a Black girl "several years older" than a little white girl caught and whipped the child that Saturday, and the child told her mother.

When the Black girl came up to the house, the mother confronted her, and the paper said the girl answered with "a direct insult." The woman then picked up a whip and gave the girl what the paper called "a genteel whipping," and the girl went home and told her parents.

About noon the girl's father went to the store of the white girl's father, and the paper said he cursed and abused the storekeeper and refused an order to leave. The storekeeper then struck him on the head with an ax handle, a blow the paper called "a telling one," and the man left. The extent of his injury was not reported, and none of the people involved was named.

Four or five warrants were issued on Monday, 25 August, "on account of this affair," but the paper did not say who was charged. No report of arrests, a hearing or a court outcome appears in the coverage.

The Savannah Morning News ran the story on 26 August as one unheaded item in its "Georgia and Florida" column of state news. The paragraph gave only the white family's version, calling the white parents "the lady" and "the gentleman" and the Black father "that worthy". It presented both assaults as answers to provocation, saying the father "added insult to insult until it was impossible for the gentleman to stand it any longer."
No account of the episode was found in other white papers or in the Black press, so the Black family's version is not recorded.

reader.title: Americus whipping and ax-handle assault (1890)
bases: Two white individuals, a mother and later her husband, carried out separate personal assaults (a whipping, a blow with an ax handle) during a family quarrel; no mob, band or crowd is reported (A1).
One paragraph in the Savannah Morning News is the only report found in either press (A1).

accounts.label: Savannah Morning News state-news paragraph (white family's version)
accounts.gist: The Black girl whipped a younger white child and insulted the child's mother, who then whipped her; the girl's father cursed the white father in his store, would not leave, and was struck with an ax handle. Warrants followed.

framing.detail: Presents each assault as a response to provocation ('added insult to insult until it was impossible for the gentleman to stand it'), calls the whipping 'genteel', and gives the Black family no voice.

record_check.dossier: Two separate assaults by two white individuals (mother, father); no mob or group is reported

record_check.record: a white storekeeper strikes a Black man with an ax handle after he curses him over the quarrel
record_check.dossier: Mostly right: the storekeeper was the white girl's father, and the man he struck was the Black girl's father. The paper also says the man refused an order to leave, and that four or five warrants were issued.
Two unnamed Black victims: a girl (whipped) and her father (struck with an ax handle)
The white girl's mother and father, unnamed
2 (the girl whipped; her father struck on the head, extent unknown)
The paper names only Americus; it gives no county

info: Saturday, 23 August 1890 (the paper of Tuesday 26 August says 'Saturday')
Americus: the white family's house and the white girl's father's store
An unnamed Black girl, described as several years older than the white child, and her unnamed father

The paper said the Black girl had caught and whipped a little white girl and then 'offered ... a direct insult' to the white girl's mother; it said the girl's father cursed and abused the white girl's father at his store and refused to leave
The white girl's mother (the whipping) and the white girl's father, a storekeeper (the blow with an ax handle); neither is named

sources.note: Only report: one paragraph in a column of Georgia and Florida news items. A white mother whipped a Black girl; the white girl's father struck the Black girl's father with an ax handle at his store; four or five warrants were issued.
quotes: In answer to the lady, the negro girl offered her a direct insult. The lady gathered up a whip which was near by and administered a genteel whipping.
At this juncture the gentleman took up an ax handle and let go at the negro's head.
Four or five warrants were issued yesterday on account of this affair.
